title: Lease Agreements for Retail Premises Bill
what_it_is: Lease Agreements for Retail Premises Bill

sections.label: Mandatory Code for retail leases
sections.summary: The Bill makes the Code's principles mandatory for leasing of all retail premises in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: We recognise that the Code enables a fair and balanced lease negotiation process that will support the growth of retail businesses and strengthen the symbiotic relationship between tenants and landlords in the long run.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: This Bill will make the principles of the Code mandatory for the leasing of all retail premises in Singapore.

sections.label: Bill's three main measures
sections.summary: The Bill mandates Code compliance, establishes the Fair Tenancy Industry Committee, and creates a dispute resolution process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Bill will: one, mandate compliance with the leasing principles in the Code; two, establish the Fair Tenancy Industry Committee and provide for its role, among other things, as custodian of the Code; and three establish an accessible and affordable dispute resolution process for parties to address matters of non-compliance.

sections.label: Tenants and landlords must comply
sections.summary: The Bill requires all tenants and landlords of retail premises to comply with the Code's leasing principles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: First, the Bill requires all tenants and all landlords of retail premises to comply with the leasing principles that are set out in the Code.

sections.label: Dispute resolution and FTIC functions
sections.summary: The Bill provides mediation and adjudication for non-compliance complaints and establishes the FTIC's functions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Bill also offers a dispute resolution process to address complaints of non-compliance with the Code's leasing principles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: So, if a landlord or tenant files a complaint of non-compliance, the parties will, first, be required to undergo mediation to resolve the dispute.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: However, if the mediation does not lead to an agreed outcome, the Bill provides for an adjudicator to be empowered to decide on the dispute.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The adjudicator will be able to order the parties to vary the lease agreement or pay compensation, where applicable, for their non-compliant conduct.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The adjudicator's determination will be enforceable as an order of the Court once permission from the Court is granted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Lastly, the Bill formally establishes the FTIC as the body appointed by the Minister for Trade and Industry to, first, periodically review and, with the Minister's approval, modify the Code; second, to monitor and promote compliance by tenants and landlords with the Act and the Code; and third, to establish the process for submission of declarations of permitted deviations from the leasing principles that are set out in the Code.

sections.label: Mandating Code with declared deviations
sections.summary: The Bill mandates key leasing principles with jointly declared permitted deviations for retail leases of one year or more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As Minister of State Ms Low has outlined, the Bill seeks to mandate compliance with the key leasing principles in the Code, with permitted deviations that have to be jointly declared by landlord and tenant for all retail lease agreements with a tenure of one year or more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It also seeks to establish the dispute resolution process and officially establish the functions of FTIC.

sections.label: Code's origin and contents
sections.summary: The Code was developed and released in 2021 by the Fair Tenancy Pro Tem Committee and contains 11 leasing principles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Code was developed and released in 2021 by the Fair Tenancy Pro Tem Committee which was formed in 2020 under the auspices of the SBF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Code contains 11 leasing principles for key tenancy terms, confidentiality clauses and data transparency.

sections.label: Data transparency leasing principle scope
sections.summary: The data transparency leasing principle applies only to landlords collecting sales data under the GTO Rent formula, with guidelines for sharing sales data metrics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Code’s data transparency leasing principle only applies to landlords who collect sales data from tenants as part of the GTO Rent formula.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The guidelines call for landlords to share sales data metrics according to trade category with existing tenants on a bi-annual basis and on a one-on-one basis before the signing of the lease agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Can I confirm with the Minister that this is true, and what is the expected percentage of qualifying leases that would require the data transparency principle to be complied with?

sections.label: Committee recommended two rental data levels
sections.summary: The Committee recommended two levels of rental data: a monthly public rental info database and mall-level data from landlords to tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Back then, the Committee shared that it recommends two levels of rental data be made available, namely, a public rental info database that is uploaded on a monthly basis, and mall-level productivity and performance data made available by landlords to tenants from whom they require data, such as monthly sales data.

sections.label: Government considering rental database, HDB leading
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government is considering such a database and whether HDB would lead by example in providing the information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Is the Government actively considering such a database and whether or not the Housing and Development Board (HDB), as one of the largest landlords of retail space, would be willing to lead by example and provide such information?

sections.label: FTIC outreach and education function
sections.summary: Clause 4E gives FTIC a function to conduct outreach and education on the Act, Code and retail leasing matters, with a request for resource details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 4E of the Bill states that one of the functions of FTIC is "to conduct outreach and education relating to this Act and the Code of Conduct and matters relating to the leasing of retail premises." I am supportive of this move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even while the code of conduct has already been introduced on a voluntary basis, smaller retailers today who lack the resources and awareness to vet through contracts could simply sign it without understanding its terms and conditions and any exceptional clauses to be wary of.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope the Minister could provide further information, such as the amount of resources dedicated to outreach and education efforts, especially for our SME retailers.

sections.label: Bridging landlord-tenant power differential
sections.summary: The passage supports the Bill for enhancing data transparency and information sharing, and hopes more is done to bridge the landlord-tenant power differential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The passing of this Bill is a step in the right direction, but by enhancing data transparency and information sharing and narrowing the gulf in information between SME tenants and retail landlords, I hope more can also be done to better effectively bridge the power differential between landlords and tenants, thus providing our smaller retailers with a better fighting chance to sustain their businesses.

sections.label: Code of conduct lease clause changes
sections.summary: Under the code of conduct, landlords cannot include clauses forcing tenants to pay unspecified costs, and both parties may pre-terminate leases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Among other things, under the code of conduct, retail landlords will no longer be allowed to include clauses in leases to force tenants to pay for unspecified costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Landlords and tenants will both have the right to pre-terminate the lease, unlike previously, when only landlords typically had this right.

sections.label: Rent share of business costs
sections.summary: Rent accounts for more than 25% of the cost of doing business in the retail and F&B sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Rent accounts for more than 25% of the cost of doing business in the retail and F&B sectors.

sections.label: Bill enforces code of conduct
sections.summary: The Bill gives teeth and enforcement power to the code of conduct by enshrining it in law and obliging all retail landlords in Singapore to come on board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill gives teeth and enforcement power to the code of conduct by enshrining it in law and obliging all retail landlords in Singapore to come on board.

sections.label: A&P and service charges
sections.summary: A question asks whether A&P and service charges under leasing principle 3.2 are based on cost recovery principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, with regard to advertising and promotion (A&P) and service charges under leasing principle 3.2, which states that the landlord is entitled to adjust the service charge and advertising and promotion charges, provided that the overall rents payable by tenants do not increase, can I clarify whether A&P and service charges are based on cost recovery principles?

sections.label: Recourse for non-compliance
sections.summary: A question asks what recourse and remedy are available if landlords do not comply with the 14-day filing requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What recourse and remedy are available if landlords do not comply with the 14-day filing requirement, especially concerning deviations in the rental model?

sections.label: Prohibition on electricity profiteering
sections.summary: The Bill strictly prohibits profiteering from the sale of electricity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Bill strictly prohibits profiteering from the sale of electricity.

sections.label: Specifying pass-through charges
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Bill can explicitly specify the types of charges that can be reasonably passed through to tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: One, can the Bill explicitly specify the types of charges that can be reasonably passed through to tenants to prevent unwarranted additional costs?

sections.label: Power imbalance in small business contracts
sections.summary: Five years ago the speaker's Adjournment Motion speech highlighted onerous contractual clauses imposed by dominant market players on small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Five years ago in this House, in my Adjournment Motion speech entitled “Power Imbalance in Contracts Involving Small Businesses”, I highlighted the onerous nature of contractual clauses which were, as a matter of course, imposed by the dominant players in the market against the small businesses.

sections.label: Government response on SME challenges
sections.summary: The Senior Minister of State for Law said the Government was empathetic to SME challenges but that free-market principles should generally apply, with intervention only when necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In response, the hon Senior Minister of State for Law, as she then was, Ms Indranee Rajah, stated that whilst the Government was, and I quote, “empathetic to the challenges faced by SMEs”, the Government’s underlying philosophy is that, quote again, “in general, free-market principles should apply and the Government should only intervene when necessary, for example, to address systemic market failures”.

sections.label: Bill marks government position shift
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Bill's introduction five years later as a significant shift in the Government's position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The introduction of this Bill, five years since, represents, in my respectful view, a significant shift in the Government’s position which I welcome.

sections.label: Bill gives teeth to Code
sections.summary: The Bill gives teeth to a Code of Conduct stating an objective to guide landlords and tenants toward fair and balanced lease negotiations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this, the Bill gives teeth to a Code of Conduct in which it is expressly stated that one key objective is to provide guidance to landlords and tenants to enable a fair and balanced position in lease negotiations.

sections.label: Dispute resolution mechanism for leasing
sections.summary: Part 4 of the Bill provides a dispute resolution mechanism for landlords or tenants complaining of non-compliance with a leasing principle in the Code of Conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Part 4 of the Bill provides the dispute resolution mechanism that may be invoked by a landlord or a tenant should there be a complaint that there has been a non-compliance with a leasing principle set out in the Code of Conduct.

sections.label: Minister may authorise dispute body
sections.summary: Under clause 10 of the Bill, the Minister may authorise any person to be an authorised dispute resolution body.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under clause 10 of the Bill, the Minister may authorise any person to be an authorised dispute resolution body.

sections.label: Adjudicator determination on leasing principle
sections.summary: Under clause 25(4), the adjudicator must determine whether a leasing principle has been breached.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under clause 25 (4) of the Bill, the adjudicator must make a determination whether there has been a non-compliance with a leasing principle.

sections.label: Setting aside adjudication determination
sections.summary: Clause 27(4) allows a party to start separate High Court proceedings to set aside the adjudication determination, subject to security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I note that there is no provision specifically providing for an appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, under clause 27(4) of the Bill, it is proposed that a party may commence separate proceedings in the General Division of the High Court to set aside the adjudication determination subject to the provision of security.

sections.label: Power imbalances and fairness in contracting
sections.summary: Power imbalances oppress small businesses and disregard the public good, while fairness, equity and autonomy in contracting achieve a win-win solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In time, we have recognised that there are power imbalances which do not work, not only because they oppress small businesses, but because they do not respect the general public good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In promoting fairness, equity and true autonomy in contracting, we achieve the rare feat of a "win-win" solution.

sections.label: SME lower rents and Rent Control Act
sections.summary: His speech said the member sought lower rents for SMEs, which triggered memories of the Rent Control Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: What I said in my speech was that he sought lower rents on behalf of SMEs and, as a result of that, it triggered memories of the Rent Control Act.

sections.label: Tenant and landlord collaboration in Committee
sections.summary: A collaborative effort between tenant and landlords in the Committee is needed to produce win-win situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The point I made, which does not really need me to repeat, is that, at the end of the day, we need to have a collaborative effort between the tenant and the landlords in the context of the Committee to come up with win-win situations.

sections.label: No rent control insinuation, consensual Committee approach
sections.summary: He made no insinuation about rent control to Mr Leong, but addressed the point on low rents and the Bill's consensual Committee approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Well, Sir, I mean, without getting into the emotion of things, let me just assure my hon friend, Mr Leong, that I was not making any specific insinuation about rent control to him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I was just picking up a point that he made in the course of his speech, where he advocated that in light of rent-seeking behaviours of landlords, there should be efforts to make sure that tenants get low rents – I was dealing with that point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: And in that context, I spoke about the mechanism in this Bill which advocates a consensual approach – the Committee itself has representatives from the landlords, tenants and also other neutral parties.

sections.label: Self-employed support retail lease Bill
sections.summary: Self-employed business owners support the Bill, which sets guidelines for fairer lease negotiations and deters landlords from terminating leases over sales performance.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some of these businesses belong to self-employed persons who are also members of NTUC's associations for coaches and instructors and creative professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These self-employed business owners support the Bill as the Bill sets out guidelines enabling fairer lease negotiations between retail landlords and tenants.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill also deters landlords from terminating lease agreements because of sales performance.

sections.label: Post-pandemic rental increases
sections.summary: Post-pandemic, some saw steep rental increases of 15% to 40% compared with pre-COVID-19 levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Post-pandemic, some saw steep rental increase of 15% to 40%, compared with pre-COVID-19 levels.

sections.label: Retail Premises Bill step forward
sections.summary: The Lease Agreements for Retail Premises Bill is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Lease Agreements for Retail Premises Bill is a step in the right direction.

sections.label: Mandated Code of Conduct compliance
sections.summary: The Bill will mandate compliance with a Code of Conduct for certain retail leases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill will mandate compliance with a Code of Conduct for certain retail leases.

sections.label: Qualifying leases and leasing principles
sections.summary: The Bill will require qualifying retail leases to comply with the Code and 13 leasing principles under the Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill will require qualifying retail leases to comply with the Code and 13 leasing principles under the Code.

sections.label: Requirements set out in Codes
sections.summary: Requirements for qualifying retail leases will be set out under the Codes, which can be modified by the Committee with the Minister's consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The requirements that qualifying retail leases must comply with will be set out under the Codes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is significant that requirements are set out in the Codes that can be modified by the Committee with the Minister's consent.

sections.label: Minister exemption by Gazette order
sections.summary: Section 32 lets the Minister exempt any person or premises from the Act by Gazette order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In addition to this, section 32 allows the Minister to exempt any person or premises from the scope of the Act by order in the Gazette.

sections.label: Code of Conduct issue date
sections.summary: The Code of Conduct was drawn up and issued on 26 March 2021 by the Fair Tenancy Pro Tem Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Code of Conduct was drawn up and issued on 26 March 2021 by the Fair Tenancy Pro Tem Committee.

sections.label: Caution on Code amendments
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to review amendment requests with caution to balance landlord and tenant fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I know how difficult it is when the tenant demands hundreds of thousands of dollars for the premises that he does not own and for which he has been paying a small meagre sum of rental for many years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, I call on the Government to review any request for amendments to the Code of Conduct with some caution so that a right balance of fairness can be considered from both the landlord and the tenant's point of view.

sections.label: A&P charge capped at gross rent
sections.summary: Paragraph 3 caps the A&P charge at overall gross rent, but the speaker says A&P charges must be negotiated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Paragraph 3 of the Code of Conduct provides for Advertising and Promotion (A&P) charge to be capped at the overall gross rent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This means that if a landlord wants to adjust what is commonly known as the A&P charge, he must do so within the total gross rent payable by the tenant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But surely, A&P charges payable by a tenant must be a matter of negotiation between the landlord and tenant.

sections.label: Mandatory reminders on capex declaration
sections.summary: The speaker agrees landlords should be made to remind tenants to submit capex value declarations within three months of renovation completion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: As said earlier, I agree with this principle and I would add that we should make it mandatory for the landlord to send reminders to the tenant on the need to submit their declaration of value of capex works within three months of completion of the renovation works.

sections.label: Assistance for smaller landlords
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government intends to help smaller landlords be aware of complying with the Code of Conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: How does the Government intend to assist the smaller landlords to ensure that they are aware of the need to comply with the Code of Conduct?

sections.label: Adjudicators and filing costs
sections.summary: A Member asks whether the body can find enough experienced adjudicators for landlord-tenancy disputes and who bears the legal costs of filing to record a settlement agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And I know, for these past 12 years, it is not easy to establish a dispute resolution body which has a pool of experienced and respected adjudicators and mediators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, would this body referred to in the Bill be able to find enough adjudicators who are sufficiently experienced in landlord-tenancy disputes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Who then will bear the legal costs of filing the application to record the settlement agreement?

sections.label: Code elevated into law
sections.summary: One main aspect of the Bill is to elevate parts of the Code of Conduct for Leasing of Retail Premises into law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One main aspect of the Bill is to elevate parts of the Code of Conduct for Leasing of Retail Premises into law.

sections.label: Legislative bite to Part B
sections.summary: Clause 5 introduces the Code generally, but the Bill gives legislative bite only to Part B, requiring compliance with its leasing principles in a qualifying lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Even though clause 5 introduces the Code of Conduct generally, it appears that the Bill only gives legislative bite to Part B of the Code, by requiring the landlord and the tenant of a "qualifying lease" to comply with the leasing principles set out in Part B.

sections.label: Deviations and FTIC declaration
sections.summary: Four of the 11 leasing principles can be deviated from if landlord and tenant mutually agree, and clause 6 requires permitted deviations to be declared to FTIC or be void.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Four out of the 11 leasing principles under the Code – relating to exclusivity terms, sales performance clauses, rental structure and security deposit – can be deviated from, provided that the landlord and the tenant mutually agree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Bill also provides that any permitted deviation from the leasing principles must be declared to FTIC or else it might be void.

sections.label: Disputes mediation or court
sections.summary: A Member asks whether disputes over non-compliance with the leasing principles must always go through the Bill's mediation and adjudication process rather than a Court or arbitral tribunal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Does this also mean that disputes over non-compliance with the leasing principles must always be subject to the mediation and adjudication process under the Bill, and cannot be decided by a Court or arbitral tribunal?

sections.label: Rent review in other countries
sections.summary: The passage describes rent revision mechanisms in France, Belgium and Australian states, and suggests FTIC or the Ministry may wish to look into this area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In France, the law provides for a legal mechanism where the rent will be revised every three years based on an index without recourse to the courts, following a request from the landlord or the tenant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In Belgium, a party may apply to court to obtain an adjustment of the rent where there are new circumstances affecting the normal rental value of the leased building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In various Australian states, the law prescribes certain restrictions on the rent review procedure and calculation methodology that may be agreed by the parties in the lease agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This may be an area that FTIC or the Ministry may wish to look into going forward.

sections.label: Mandating Code of Conduct compliance
sections.summary: Mandating compliance with the Code of Conduct will ensure all retail sectors and tenants are covered and benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Although some landlords had voluntarily adopted the Code of Conduct, mandating compliance with the Code will ensure that all retail sectors and tenants will be covered and will benefit from it.

sections.label: Public footfall and rental data
sections.summary: Monthly updated footfall and average rental per square foot by mall, building or floor should be public information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Monthly updated information on footfall and the average rental per square foot by mall, building or floor, should be public information, just like for residential properties as well.

sections.label: Lease review costs and FTIC
sections.summary: Lawyer fees for lease review can cost $1,000 to $3,000, and the speaker asks about other accessible communication channels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For example, it can cost $1,000 to $3,000 to engage a lawyer to review and amend a lease agreement, which can be quite significant for some businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Apart from FTIC and the Singapore Mediation Centre (SMC), are there other communication channels which are convenient and accessible to small businesses?

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Please allow me to address the points raised in the course of my speech.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: As before, for the sake of clarity, I will refer to the Fair Tenancy Industry Committee established under this Bill as FTIC, and the Fair Tenancy Industry Committee that was formed two years ago in May 2021 as "current Committee" in my speech.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In June 2020, when we first embarked on the journey to strengthen the retail sector with tenant and landlord representatives from the Pro Tem Committee, to be honest, it was far from certain that any common ground could be found, let alone a full-fledged and robust Code of Conduct that we have before us today in the House for this debate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: So, the Code was, in the words of a current Committee member, and I quote her, "a landmark for the industry" and it is "a miracle that we could even reach this stage".

sections.label: No mark-ups on electricity costs
sections.summary: The aim is to improve transparency and make clear landlords cannot charge mark-ups on electricity costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: What we want here is to improve transparency and to promote fair practices to make it clear that the landlord cannot charge mark-ups on electricity costs.

sections.label: A&P charges and Code principles
sections.summary: A&P charges are landlord business costs subsumed in gross rent, and data transparency principles bring the total to 13.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Rather, the Code holds the position that A&P charges are considered as business costs incurred by landlords and should thus be subsumed in the overall gross rent, rather than be borne fully by tenants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The current Committee has updated the draft Code to raise the bar on data transparency and confidentiality and elevated the status of data transparency and confidentiality guidelines to be leasing principles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: This brings the total number of principles to 13, instead of 11, which the Bill mandates compliance with.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The draft Code will be finalised in the coming months and will take effect on the same day as the date of commencement of the Act in early February 2024.

sections.label: Bill scope and exemptions
sections.summary: The Government intends the Bill to apply to all retail premises with a lease tenure of one year or more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the scope of the Bill and how might the Minister exercise the power to exempt specific persons or premises from the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to assure him that the Government intends for the Bill to apply to all retail premises with a lease tenure of one year or more.

sections.label: Unfiled permitted deviations consequences
sections.summary: Unfiled permitted deviations on exclusivity, sales performance and security deposit make the deviation void, while an unfiled rental formula deviation keeps the same formula.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In cases where permitted deviations on exclusivity, sales performance and security deposit fail to be filed – to answer Members' questions – the deviation in the lease agreement would be void and the default position, as stated in the Code, would then apply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For the fourth scenario, for the fourth leasing principle where deviation is allowed, where it concerns the rental formula, if the permitted deviation related to the rental formula fails to be filed, the lease will continue on the same rental formula.

sections.label: Bill mandates 13 leasing principles
sections.summary: The Bill is before Parliament to mandate compliance with the industry-led Code's 13 leasing principles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The reason why we are coming to Parliament today to pass this Bill to support this industry-led Code is to mandate compliance with the 13 leasing principles.

sections.label: Whichever is higher rental formula
sections.summary: Tenants may deviate to a "whichever is higher" rental formula, which the Code permits only by mutual agreement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Certain tenants may want to deviate and opt for a "whichever is higher" rental formula, which is currently not permitted in the Code, except by mutual agreement.

sections.label: Mediators and adjudicators qualifications
sections.summary: The panel of mediators and adjudicators appointed by the Singapore Mediation Centre will be fully qualified on Code non-compliance matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Because out of the three speakers, two are legally trained, I want to assure them that the panel of mediators and adjudicators appointed by the authorised dispute resolution body, which will be the Singapore Mediation Centre, SMC for short, will be fully qualified to deal with matters of non-compliance with the Code.

sections.label: Adjudicator variation or compensation orders
sections.summary: The adjudicator can determine a variation of the lease or order compensation if the leasing principle provides for compensation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The adjudicator can either determine a variation of the lease or order a compensation, if the leasing principle in question provides for compensation to be made.

sections.label: Dispute resolution in addition to redress
sections.summary: The Bill's mediation and adjudication framework is provided in addition to any other redress parties have outside the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: While we encourage parties to use the mediation and adjudication services that are set out in the Bill for Code-related complaints, this dispute resolution framework is provided, in addition to any other redress that the parties would have outside of the Bill.

sections.label: Code compliance for tenants landlords
sections.summary: The Code addresses structural industry issues and enables long-term partnerships, and the Bill will mandate that all tenants and landlords comply with it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The Code addresses structural issues in the industry and enables both parties to forge long-term symbiotic partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: This Bill will mandate that all tenants and landlords comply with the Code.

sections.label: Lease template for heartland shopowners
sections.summary: FMAS is developing a lease agreement template tailored for heartland shopowners and will launch it by this year-end.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: FMAS is also developing a lease agreement template tailored for heartland shopowners and will launch it by this year-end.

sections.label: Updated Code effective date
sections.summary: The updated Code is expected to take effect on the same day as the commencement of the Act in early February next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The updated Code is expected to take effect on the same day as the commencement of the Act in early February next year.

sections.label: Code as living document
sections.summary: The Code is a living document and will continue to evolve to meet the needs of the industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: To conclude, I would like to reiterate that the Code is a living document and will continue to evolve to meet the needs of the industry.
